title: Starbucks to Close 250 Stores in North America
paragraphs: Starbucks has announced that it will close about 250 of its stores in North America, marking the coffee giant's second major wave of closures in two years.

The company announced the decision on September 24, saying the stores would close that week. The closures represent roughly 1% of the more than 18,000 Starbucks locations in the region. However, the company has not revealed which stores are affected, or how many are in the United States and how many are in Canada.

Mike Grams, the company's chief operating officer, said the decision followed a review of its North American stores. According to Grams, the stores being closed either could not consistently provide the experience the company wanted for customers and employees, or did not have a path toward "acceptable financial performance."

The move is part of a wider restructuring plan led by CEO Brian Niccol, who took charge of the company in 2024. Last September, Starbucks closed 627 stores in North America and Europe and laid off 900 employees who did not work in stores.

Starbucks says employees at the affected stores will be offered jobs at other locations where possible. Those who cannot be transferred will receive severance support. The union representing workers at unionized Starbucks stores criticized the move, saying that closures at unionized locations should be subject to collective bargaining.

Despite the closures, Starbucks insists that it remains committed to growing in North America. In fact, recent results suggest its business is improving. Comparable store sales in North America rose 8.1% in the most recent quarter.
However, the company is also reducing its plans for new stores. In a filing, it said it would open around 440 new stores in fiscal year 2026, fewer than the 600 to 650 it had previously planned.
